Online appendix · Product Relatedness in Tasks

Product-product similarity in occupations

Interactive counterpart to Figure 4 of the paper. Each cell is the directional task similarity Φ(ω, ω′) between two HS4 products' occupational task vectors, weighted by asymmetric skill transferability estimated from worker flows between occupations. Origin products ω are in rows and destination products ω′ in columns, so the matrix is not symmetric: Φ(ω, ω′) and Φ(ω′, ω) can differ. Values closer to 1 (bright yellow) indicate products whose production draws on very similar occupations; values closer to 0 (dark blue) indicate little occupational overlap. The diagonal equals 1 by construction. Only products satisfying GDPR thresholds (more than five single-product firms observed, 2010–2019) are included. Hover over any tile to see the two HS4 product codes, their names, and the similarity in both directions.

120 products · 14,280 directional pairs · colour scale: viridis, γ = 1.5

Download the data

The full directional similarity matrix (rows = origin ω, columns = destination ω′) and a tidy pairwise version are available below. The pairwise file has one row per product pair, sorted by similarity: the origin is the product in the direction with the higher value, and the reverse direction is reported in the last column.
